messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The test case `testExactOptionNameMatch` fails because when parsing the argument `--prefix` the parser tries to match the long option name exactly. Examining the `DefaultParser.parse` method and its helper methods shows that parsing involves token handling via the `handleToken` method. Specifically for long options (arguments that start with `--`), the parser calls `handleLongOption`, which distinguishes whether the token contains an `=` or not. In the case without an equal sign, the parser calls `handleLongOptionWithoutEqual`.

Inside `handleLongOptionWithoutEqual`, the code uses `options.getMatchingOptions(token)` to find matching long options. This method strips leading hyphens first, then gathers all registered long options that start with the stripped token string. If there is exactly one match, parsing continues; if there is more than one match, an `AmbiguousOptionException` is thrown.

The problem stems from the prefix matching logic in `Options.getMatchingOptions`: it considers all options whose long option string *starts with* the given token as matches. This behavior causes issues if one long option is a prefix of another distinct long option, leading to false ambiguity detection (as described in the current bug report "LongOpt falsely detected as ambiguous"). For example, `--import` and `--importToOpen` cause an ambiguous match on `--import`, which is supposed to match exactly to `--import` but is mistranslated as ambiguous because both options start with `import`.

Thus, the root cause is that `Options.getMatchingOptions` does prefix matching on long options without considering exact matches first, causing false ambiguous exceptions when long options share common prefixes but the user's intention is an exact match.

This behavior explains the test failure, as the test likely has overlapping option names sharing prefixes and expects exact matching to succeed without ambiguity errors.

No recent bug reports are related or suggest fixes to this functionality, so the diagnosis is made primarily from the current bug and source code. The fault lies in the `Options.getMatchingOptions` method's prefix-based matching logic.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
